title: KenRex will be playing at the Lucille Lortel through June 27th, and I...
transcript: everyone's buzzing about the award winning true crime thriller that just transferred to New York after multiple hit runs in the U K and I think the hype is very well deserved for my money it even features the best score of the season so far and it's not even a musical created by Jack Holden and Ed Stambollouian KenRex tells the true story of Ken Rex Mcelroy a man who spent years terrorizing a small Missouri town without facing legal consequences and it's told here from the perspective of the prosecutor in Ken Rex's final case where it's framed like as his testimonial where he plays all the roles aside from capturing the audience's attention with edge of your seat suspense the production is also a technical marvel not necessarily in terms of scale or innovation but all the design elements especially the sound and the lighting just very cleverly augment the storytelling and so impressively synchronized with the performers voice and movements to elevate this relatively simple play into what feels like a high wire spectacle at an off Broadway scale but even more thrilling is the incidental music which is written and performed live by John Patrick Elliott it's like a jolt of lightning through the show with a haunting, propulsive country inspired sound that echoes the deep disquiet that this whole community and the narrator feel in the face of this seemingly unstoppable threat throughout the play I did find myself wondering if the character of Ken Rex, as he's portrayed here, is a little bit too much of like a clean and simple villain kind of a one dimensional boogeyman. not that I needed a redemption arc or a tear-jerking villain origin story but because the play already dances around these themes of community responsibility and ethics it might have warranted just a bit more examination of who this clearly very troubled and complicated person actually was having said that the writers do find a way in the end to subvert the audience's perspective leaving us with a nagging sense of moral uncertainty about how the situation ended. so in the end the play does have that edge of nuance that I was looking for just in a way I wasn't expecting.
classificationReason: Creator shares first-hand opinions praising the show ('hype is very well deserved', 'best score of the season'), detailing performance, sound, lighting, and music elements.
